deep.reconstruction:
This is page 1 of a lecture plan titled 'Cohomologie de De Rham des var. alg.', dated Nov.–Déc. 1966, with the last digit overwritten in red. It is almost certainly the outline of Grothendieck's IHES lectures of December 1966, written up by J. Coates and O. Jussila as 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés sur la cohomologie des schémas, 1968). The archive folder 'laïus ... (Cristaux)' fits this.

Stated aim: convey a cluster of problems around the de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties, and propose a viewpoint that groups them, giving a '(gros) programme de travail'.

§1 'Yoga' of de Rham cohomology, in three steps.
(1) Smooth manifolds. The de Rham theorem is explained sheaf-theoretically. The de Rham complex Ω^·_X resolves the constant sheaf C_X (Poincaré lemma). Each Ω^i_X is fine, hence acyclic in positive degrees. Therefore H*(X,C) is the cohomology of the complex of global forms Γ(X,Ω^·).
(2) Complex analytic manifolds. The holomorphic Poincaré lemma still holds locally, so Ω^·_X resolves C_X. The sheaves Ω^p are no longer fine. The naive argument therefore works only when H^q(X,Ω^p)=0 for q>0, e.g. on Stein manifolds (Cartan's Theorem B). In general one must use hypercohomology: H*(X,C) ≅ ℍ*(X,Ω^·_X). This is computed by the Hodge-to-de Rham (Frölicher) spectral sequence E_1^{pq}=H^q(X,Ω^p_X) ⇒ H^{p+q}(X,C).
(3) Smooth complex algebraic varieties with the Zariski topology. Define algebraic de Rham cohomology as the Zariski hypercohomology ℍ*(X,Ω^·_{X/C}). Question: is it isomorphic to H*(X^an,C)? There is always a natural map ℍ*(X,Ω^·_X) → ℍ*(X^an,Ω^·_{X^an}) ≅ H*(X^an,C).

The next page answers that this map is an isomorphism (Grothendieck's comparison theorem). For affine X this gives singular cohomology from global algebraic forms. The proper case follows from GAGA applied termwise to the Hodge spectral sequences. The general case uses resolution of singularities.
errors: In (1) the acyclicity of fine sheaves needs X paracompact Hausdorff, not merely 'séparé'. This is a harmless abbreviation, since manifolds are usually assumed paracompact.

No substantive mathematical errors on this page. (On the next page the theorem is stated for 'préschéma loc. de type fini' without explicitly repeating smoothness. Smoothness is needed for the naive algebraic de Rham complex, but it is assumed in heading 3 'non singulières'.)

ideas.what: Sheaf-theoretic proof of de Rham's theorem: Poincaré lemma plus fineness of Ω^i
ideas.modern_name: de Rham theorem via acyclic resolutions
ideas.where_published: Standard (Godement, Tôhoku-era sheaf theory); not specifically Grothendieck's

ideas.what: For complex manifolds, H*(X,C)=ℍ*(X,Ω^·) with the Hodge-to-de Rham (Frölicher) spectral sequence E_1^{pq}=H^q(Ω^p)
ideas.modern_name: Holomorphic de Rham theorem / Frölicher spectral sequence
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'On the de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties', Publ. Math. IHES 29 (1966)

ideas.what: Algebraic de Rham cohomology as Zariski hypercohomology of Ω^·_{X/C}, with the comparison map to H*(X^an,C)
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck's algebraic de Rham comparison theorem
ideas.where_published: Publ. Math. IHES 29 (1966); 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes', Dix exposés (1968)

deep.surprise_reason: This is the opening outline of a lecture course whose content (the comparison theorem and the crystalline programme) is published, in Publ. IHES 29 and in the Coates–Jussila notes in Dix exposés. The page contains only standard material, framed pedagogically.
transcription_corrections: 'Se transpose tel quel pour les Stein' more likely reads 'Ça marche tel quel pour les Stein'.
In item (1) the parenthetical reads '(lemme de Poincaré)'. In item (2) '(local)' is inserted above, giving 'lemme de Poincaré (local) valable'.
Date: the last digit of 'Nov. Déc. 196_' is overwritten in red. It plausibly reads 1966, consistent with the December 1966 IHES lectures.
The isomorphism symbol under H*(X,C) is a vertical '≀' (≅) linking it to ℍ*(X,Ω^·_X), not '12'.
